newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper, aluminium, zinc stocks seen down-trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, aluminium, zinc stocks seen down-trade.

text.p: Stocks on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are expected to show an overall decline later on Friday with copper seen leading the fall by 5,000 tonnes, Singapore base metal traders said.
Aluminium stocks were expected to be down by 2,000 tonnes and zinc by between 1,000-3,000 tonnes, they said.
Despite the forecast decline in overall LME zinc inventories, stocks in the exchange's warehouse in Singapore may increase by around 3,000 tonnes.
A dealer said as much as 20,000 tonnes of Chinese zinc maybe heading towards the city-state with the bulk of the supplies sold to a European trade house.
The volume of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse on Tuesday reached 38,650 tonnes, down 125 tonnes from the previous report.
Three-month LME copper was quoted around $2,269/$2,274 a tonne at 0400 GMT, up slightly from London's close on Thursday.
Traders said the market is likely to hover between $2,240-$2,280 in the short term.
Cash copper was quoted at around $2,570 a tonne. Traders said the market would be watching the backwardation, the premium of spot over forward prices, very closely.
On Thursday, the backwardation in the London market rose to $290/$295 a tonne up from $234-$238 earlier this week.
